data.one_liner: Cross-platform local notifications plugin supporting Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
data.what_it_does: Provides a unified facade for managing and showing local notifications and chat-style messages with interactive actions across multiple operating systems. It handles platform initialization, payload delivery, notification cancellation, and user action streams.
use_when: You need to display standard local notifications or chat-style notifications across Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Your app needs to handle click events, reply actions, or mark-as-read actions via a unified stream.
You want to target both JavaScript and WebAssembly on web browsers using the native Browser Notifications API.
avoid_when: You require server-driven push notifications or background messaging handlers that persist reliably after app termination without custom native setup.
You are targeting mobile web browsers requiring service-worker notifications (such as iOS browsers).
strengths: Comprehensive cross-platform support including mobile, desktop, and web.
Includes built-in chat-style notifications and interactive actions on Android with standard fallbacks on other platforms.
Provides a unified stream API for actions like clicks, replies, and mark-as-read.
weaknesses: Does not persist or replay actions after app termination without custom native configuration.
Web backend is page-scoped and requires the page to stay open to receive clicks.
data.setup_notes: Requires platform-specific configuration such as adding an action broadcast receiver in the Android manifest, setting notification center delegates on iOS and macOS, and ensuring proper desktop server/identity setup on Windows and Linux.
